metas.name: Hoop Dreams
metas.description: Captures the American dream as a system that uses kids up. Two Chicago teenagers filmed over five years chasing basketball as a way out, as school, family, money and injury keep intervening.

metas.name: Paris Is Burning
metas.description: Captures people inventing family, language and glamour inside exclusion. New York ball culture — houses as chosen families, categories, voguing — joyful and blunt about race, poverty and murder.

metas.name: The Act of Killing
metas.description: Captures impunity as performance. Indonesian mass killers, never punished and locally celebrated, gleefully re-stage their killings as Hollywood genres, until one man's body reacts before his conscience does.

metas.name: Grey Gardens
metas.description: Captures a mother and daughter fused together in a decaying mansion. The Beales, relatives of Jackie Kennedy, singing, bickering and feeding raccoons in the attic — performing for the camera and trapped with each other.

metas.name: Harlan County, USA
metas.description: Captures a labour strike from inside the picket line. Kentucky coal miners, their wives taking over the fight, company gunmen driving past at night — filmed as it happened, over years.

metas.name: Flee
metas.description: Captures telling a hidden life story for the first time. An animated documentary about a refugee from Afghanistan settled in Denmark, recounting flight, family separation and a secret he has kept from everyone.

metas.name: Stop Making Sense
metas.description: Captures a band building joy in real time. A Talking Heads concert that starts with David Byrne alone with a boombox and adds one musician per song until the stage is full — and his suit keeps getting bigger.

metas.name: Amazing Grace
metas.description: Captures singing as spiritual labour. Aretha Franklin recording a live gospel album in a Los Angeles church in 1972, over two nights, in a performance that visibly costs her something.

metas.name: Summer of Soul
metas.description: Captures a community's archive left in a basement for 50 years. The 1969 Harlem Cultural Festival — Stevie Wonder, Nina Simone, Mahalia Jackson, Sly Stone — in footage almost nobody saw.

metas.name: The Last Waltz
metas.description: Captures a musical era ending on stage, politely. The Band's farewell concert with everyone they came up with as guests, and backstage interviews with men who sound relieved and bereaved at once.

metas.name: Buena Vista Social Club
metas.description: Captures old musicians being found again. Elderly Cuban son musicians, some retired to shining shoes, recording and touring — the pleasure is in their faces and Havana's streets.

metas.name: 20 Feet from Stardom
metas.description: Captures the voices you know best belonging to people you can't name. Backup singers for the Stones, Springsteen and Sting — huge talent, a career spent three steps behind someone else.

metas.name: Microcosmos
metas.description: Captures a meadow as an alien world, at insect scale. One day in a French field, almost no narration: snails mating, a dung beetle rolling its ball uphill, rain arriving like artillery.

metas.name: Koyaanisqatsi
metas.description: Captures civilisation as pattern. No dialogue or characters: time-lapse clouds, highways, factories, demolition and crowds cut to Philip Glass, until modern life starts to look like weather.

metas.name: Leviathan
metas.description: Captures commercial fishing as a sensory ordeal. Cameras strapped to nets, chains, helmets and the hull of a North Atlantic trawler — fish heads, gulls, diesel, men half-asleep at 3 a.m., no explanation offered.

metas.name: Senna
metas.description: Captures speed, faith and charisma, entirely from archive. Ayrton Senna's career built only from period footage and voices — rivalry with Prost, Brazil on his helmet, in-car laps that feel like prayer at 300 km/h.

metas.name: Free Solo
metas.description: Captures a man whose relationship to fear is simply different from yours. Alex Honnold prepares to climb El Capitan without ropes while the filmmakers — his friends — argue on camera about whether filming changes the odds.

metas.name: When We Were Kings
metas.description: Captures Ali as a political and verbal artist at his peak. The Rumble in the Jungle, Zaire 1974: training footage, a music festival, Mobutu's stadium, and Ali talking everyone, including himself, into belief.

metas.name: Jiro Dreams of Sushi
metas.description: Captures mastery as repetition across a lifetime. An 85-year-old with a tiny Tokyo subway sushi counter and three Michelin stars, sons waiting to inherit, and a standard of 'delicious' he says he still hasn't reached.

metas.name: Man with a Movie Camera
metas.description: Captures a city inventing cinema while cinema invents the city. A Soviet day from waking to work to leisure, no story, and editing tricks in every minute that films still use — nearly a century old and showing off.

metas.name: Sans Soleil
metas.description: Captures memory as footage you keep re-narrating. A woman reads a travelling cameraman's letters over images of Tokyo, Guinea-Bissau, Iceland and San Francisco, until a travel film becomes a film about how a mind stores the world.

metas.name: Los Angeles Plays Itself
metas.description: Captures a city through the lies movies told about it. A video essay built entirely from clips — how Los Angeles is used as backdrop, villain and stand-in for everywhere else — narrated by a resident who loves it and resents all of it.

metas.name: News from Home
metas.description: Captures emigration as long shots and your mother's voice. New York — subways, diners, empty streets — while her mother's letters from Brussels, full of family news and worry, are read over it; homesickness with the geography reversed.

metas.name: Stories We Tell
metas.description: Captures a family discovering its central story has an author problem. Sarah Polley interviews her own family about her late mother; the accounts agree on the love and diverge on everything else, then the film shows you its own construction.

metas.name: Honeyland
metas.description: Captures a whole economy in one woman's beehives. A Macedonian beekeeper lives by one rule — take half the honey, leave half — until new neighbours arrive who take everything. A documentary that plays like an unscripted parable.

metas.name: Night and Fog
metas.description: Captures the Holocaust through the quiet, empty camps a decade later rather than footage of the killing itself: grass growing over atrocity, and how quickly a society decides to move on. Resnais' 32-minute essay remains documentary's foundational act of memory.

metas.name: Chronicle of a Summer
metas.description: Captures the moment documentary stopped pretending the camera wasn't in the room. Rouch and Morin ask Parisians 'Are you happy?', then film themselves arguing over whether the answers were real — cinéma vérité examining its own honesty.

metas.name: Titicut Follies
metas.description: Captures what an institution does to people when nobody outside is watching. Wiseman inside a Massachusetts asylum for the criminally insane: no narration, no interviews, no mercy — a film banned for decades for what it showed.

metas.name: Salesman
metas.director: Albert Maysles, David Maysles, Charlotte Zwerin
metas.description: Captures a man whose self-belief is running out, one rejected doorstep at a time. The Maysles brothers follow a Bible salesman through Boston and Florida as his pitch slowly stops working and the road stops feeling like hope.

metas.name: Gimme Shelter
metas.director: Albert Maysles, David Maysles, Charlotte Zwerin
metas.description: Captures the precise frame where the 1960s dream curdles: Altamont, a fan stabbed to death in front of the stage, and the Rolling Stones afterwards watching the footage of it, not knowing what to say.

metas.name: Hearts and Minds
metas.description: Captures how a country talks itself into a war and then can't talk itself out of the damage. Vietnam told by everyone it passed through — generals, pilots, Vietnamese villagers, American POWs and grieving parents.

metas.name: Burden of Dreams
metas.description: Captures obsession becoming indistinguishable from the thing it depicts. Les Blank films Werner Herzog dragging a steamship over an Amazonian mountain to make Fitzcarraldo, losing his mind in exactly the way his character does.

metas.name: Shoah
metas.description: Captures memory itself as evidence. Nine and a half hours with not one frame of archival footage — only survivors, bystanders and perpetrators talking in the present tense, in the places where it happened. The most demanding film in the collection.

metas.name: The Thin Blue Line
metas.description: Captures how 'eyewitness truth' is mostly people confidently describing things that never happened. Errol Morris reconstructs a policeman's murder through conflicting accounts and stylised re-enactments — and the film's evidence helped free the man convicted of it.

metas.name: Crumb
metas.description: Captures how the same upbringing produces a famous artist, a broken man, and something in between. Cartoonist R. Crumb and his two brothers, all shaped by one brutal household, in Terry Zwigoff's unsparing family portrait.

metas.name: American Movie
metas.description: Captures delusion and genuine talent living in the same person. Mark Borchardt, a Wisconsin sanitation worker with debts and a drinking problem, tries to finish a horror short to fund his dream feature — very funny until, suddenly, it isn't.

metas.name: The Gleaners and I
metas.description: Captures resourcefulness as a whole philosophy of life, at the gentlest possible intensity. Agnès Varda follows people who live off what's left behind — fields, markets, bins — and turns her little digital camera on her own ageing hands.

metas.name: Capturing the Friedmans
metas.description: Captures a family performing normality for a camera while everything underneath it collapses. A family accused of horrific crimes, told largely through their own compulsive home videos, which keep contradicting the legal case and each other.

metas.name: The Fog of War
metas.description: Captures a brilliant man half-confessing to catastrophe. Robert McNamara, architect of Vietnam escalation, now in his eighties, lays out eleven lessons from his life in power — you decide whether the other half is honesty or self-defence.

metas.name: Grizzly Man
metas.description: Captures a man narrating himself into a story nature never agreed to be part of. Herzog assembles Timothy Treadwell's own footage: thirteen summers living among Alaskan bears he insisted loved him, before one of them killed him.

metas.name: Dear Zachary: A Letter to a Son About His Father
metas.description: Captures grief and legal-system failure like nothing else here. It begins as a film for a baby about the father he'll never meet, murdered before he was born — then the case takes a turn mid-production that is almost unbearable.

metas.name: Man on Wire
metas.description: Captures pure, pointless, joyful daring — a crime with no victim and no motive except beauty. Philippe Petit's 1974 tightrope walk between the Twin Towers, told like a heist film by the crew who smuggled the rigging up.

metas.name: Nostalgia for the Light
metas.description: Captures two kinds of searching for the past happening in the same frame. In Chile's Atacama desert, astronomers scan the sky for the universe's origins while women sift the same soil for the bones of Pinochet's disappeared.

metas.name: The Imposter
metas.description: Captures how badly people want a story to be true. A missing Texas teenager 'returns' three years later, older and with a French accent — and his family accepts him. The man himself explains exactly how he did it.

metas.name: Citizenfour
metas.description: Captures history happening at the speed of a man checking over his shoulder. Laura Poitras was already filming when Edward Snowden contacted her, so the leak of the century unfolds in a Hong Kong hotel room in real time.

metas.name: Amy
metas.description: Captures the machinery of fame eating a person whose talent is right there on screen the whole time. Amy Winehouse's rise and destruction assembled from home video, voicemails and the tabloid footage that hunted her.

metas.name: Fire at Sea
metas.description: Captures the surreal normality of living next door to catastrophe. Lampedusa, where Europe's refugee crisis washes ashore, filmed alongside the utterly ordinary life of a local boy slingshotting cacti and listening to the radio.

metas.name: I Am Not Your Negro
metas.description: Captures a writer so precise that footage from decades after his death still fits his sentences. James Baldwin's unfinished manuscript on the murders of Medgar Evers, Malcolm X and Martin Luther King, read over a century of American images.

metas.name: O.J.: Made in America
metas.description: Captures a whole country's contradictions in one man's story. Nearly eight hours, and not really about a murder trial: Los Angeles, race, celebrity and policing across fifty years, with Simpson as the thread running through all of it.

metas.name: Faces Places
metas.description: Captures art as an excuse to pay attention to people — the lightest, warmest film in this batch. Varda, 88 and going blind, tours rural France with photographer JR, pasting giant portraits of villagers onto their own villages.

metas.name: Minding the Gap
metas.description: Captures the moment a documentarian has to point the camera at himself. Bing Liu films his skateboarder friends in their rust-belt hometown over years, then slowly realises the film is about the violence they all grew up in — including his own.

metas.name: Apollo 11
metas.description: Captures the sheer procedural calm of the Moon landing. Rebuilt entirely from restored 70mm footage and audio — no narration, no talking heads — just thousands of people doing small jobs correctly until a man is standing on the Moon.

metas.name: For Sama
metas.description: Captures war from inside a family instead of inside a news report. Waad Al-Kateab films five years of the siege of Aleppo as a letter to her baby daughter, explaining why they stayed.

metas.name: Collective
metas.description: Captures corruption being dismantled in real time, and it plays like a thriller. After a Bucharest nightclub fire, burn victims start dying of infections in Romanian hospitals — and a sports newspaper, of all things, uncovers why.

metas.name: Dick Johnson Is Dead
metas.description: Captures dying approached with slapstick, tenderness and total honesty at once. Kirsten Johnson stages elaborate fake deaths for her psychiatrist father, who has dementia, so the two of them can rehearse losing each other.

metas.name: Fire of Love
metas.description: Captures a love story where the third party is the Earth itself. Volcanologists Katia and Maurice Krafft filmed each other at the edge of eruptions for twenty years, knowing the work would probably kill them. It did, together, in 1991.

metas.name: 20 Days in Mariupol
metas.description: Captures the 2022 siege of Mariupol as the people inside it actually experienced its first twenty days. AP journalists trapped in the city keep filming because getting the footage out is the only thing that makes staying mean anything.

metas.name: The Emperor's Naked Army Marches On
metas.description: Captures one man's war that never ended: veteran Kenzo Okuzaki tours Japan forcing his former officers to answer on camera for executions and cannibalism in New Guinea, while director Kazuo Hara's crew effectively enlists in his campaign.

metas.name: Extreme Private Eros: Love Song 1974
metas.description: Captures a filmmaker turning his merciless method on himself: Hara follows his ex-wife, radical feminist Miyuki Takeda, through lovers, communes and an unassisted birth, while his new partner records the sound — intimacy documented past every comfortable limit.

metas.name: Goodbye CP
metas.description: Captures subjects seizing the documentary itself: activists with cerebral palsy refuse every framing offered them, demanding to be looked at directly and confronting Hara's camera about what it wants from them.

metas.name: A Man Vanishes
metas.description: Captures a documentary dissolving into fiction: Imamura investigates a missing salesman, but the fiancée and the lead actress fall for each other, and he pulls the set apart on camera to admit the investigation has become something else.

metas.name: A
metas.description: Captures the banal interior of a demonised group: Mori films young Aum Shinrikyo believers doing chores after the sarin attack, sincere and confused, while the media siege outside performs its own hysteria.

metas.name: Minamata: The Victims and Their World
metas.description: Captures resistance as a way of life: Tsuchimoto lives with Minamata's mercury-poisoned fishing families as they confront the Chisso corporation, sit in at shareholder meetings and refuse, for years, to go away.

metas.name: The Look of Silence
metas.description: Captures confrontation inverted: Adi, whose brother was murdered in Indonesia's 1965 purges, visits the killers under cover of eye exams and asks about the killings to their faces — no shouting, only unbearable quiet where they still hold power.

metas.name: S-21: The Khmer Rouge Killing Machine
metas.description: Captures atrocity recalled as office procedure: survivor Vann Nath brings former Tuol Sleng guards back into the prison, where they re-enact their daily routines of shackling and paperwork and find nothing dramatic in their own memories.

metas.name: Symbiopsychotaxiplasm: Take One
metas.description: Captures a production seizing itself: Greaves films actors rehearsing a breakup while his crew, instructed to film everything, records its own growing revolt against him — and the revolt becomes the film, decades before the form existed.

metas.name: Portrait of Jason
metas.description: Captures the point where performance stops protecting a man: hustler and would-be cabaret act Jason Holliday performs his life all night for Shirley Clarke's provoking camera, until the act slowly, visibly cracks.

metas.name: Warrendale
metas.description: Captures institutional care running out of composure: King's cameras live inside a Toronto home for emotionally disturbed children through tenderness, chaos and a staff member's sudden death — footage the CBC commissioned, then refused to air.

metas.name: Land Without Bread
metas.description: Captures documentary dishonesty itself: Buñuel's authoritative 'ethnography' of a destitute Spanish region stages scenes, lets animals die for the camera and lies in a straight-faced voiceover — in 1933, before the form had even settled.

metas.name: Blood of the Beasts
metas.description: Captures the calm labour beneath a city's breakfast: Franju intercuts Paris waking at dawn with slaughterhouses already methodically killing horses and calves, workers chatting through the work, in twenty unflinching minutes.

metas.name: The Act of Seeing with One's Own Eyes
metas.description: Captures the camera reduced to pure looking: Brakhage films autopsies in a Pittsburgh morgue silently and in close-up, with no commentary to hide behind, asking whether there is anything a camera should refuse to see.

metas.name: On the Bowery
metas.description: Captures neo-realist method eating its own ethics: Rogosin lived among New York's skid-row alcoholics, then had them play themselves in a story built from their lives, as the production's own drinking blurred every line.

metas.name: The House Is Black
metas.description: Captures the refusal to look away turned tender: poet Forugh Farrokhzad films inside an Iranian leper colony — classes, a wedding, prayer — reading her own poetry over faces the world had agreed not to see.

metas.name: From a Night Porter's Point of View
metas.description: Captures an authoritarian personality describing itself as common sense: Kieślowski gives a factory night porter who adores rules, informers and surveillance enough rope to explain his whole worldview, delighted with himself throughout.

metas.name: Aileen: Life and Death of a Serial Killer
metas.description: Captures the confrontational filmmaker finding his limit: Broomfield builds a real relationship with death-row killer Aileen Wuornos, testifies in her case, and films a final interview in which she is plainly no longer competent.

metas.name: The Bridge
metas.description: Captures the complicity question in its purest form: Steel filmed the Golden Gate Bridge for a year, recording suicides, without telling families what the footage was for — when the camera keeps rolling, what exactly is it doing?

metas.name: Tickled
metas.description: Captures an investigation whose subject fights back in real time: journalist David Farrier asks a cheerful question about 'competitive endurance tickling' videos and receives legal threats so disproportionate that following them becomes the film.

metas.name: Cameraperson
metas.description: Captures a career of looking, reckoned with: Kirsten Johnson cuts decades of outtakes from other people's difficult documentaries — Bosnia, Darfur, her own mother's decline — into a memoir about what pointing a camera at someone's worst day costs.

metas.name: Icarus
metas.description: Captures a documentary swallowed by its own story: Fogel films himself doping to expose how easy cheating is, but his Russian scientist accomplice sits at the centre of a state doping programme, and the film becomes his escape plan.

metas.name: Strong Island
metas.description: Captures grief conducted as cross-examination: Yance Ford investigates his brother's killing and the grand jury that declined to indict, addressing the camera directly and interrogating his own family's silence as hard as the legal system's.

metas.name: The Battle of Chile
metas.description: Captures a revolution and its destruction filmed by people unsure which they were recording: Guzmán's crew shoots Allende's final year in Chile's streets across three parts, as mass rallies and strikes give way to the coup arriving around the camera.

metas.name: Baraka
metas.description: Captures humanity as a planetary process. Shot in 70mm across 24 countries with no narration and no plot — prayer, factories, volcanoes, crowds moving like weather systems — beautiful and faintly horrifying in the same shots.

metas.name: Winged Migration
metas.director: Jacques Perrin, Jacques Cluzaud, Michel Debats
metas.description: Captures migration from the bird's side of it. Cameras fly inside migrating flocks over years and continents, close enough to hear wingbeats — endurance as the most ordinary thing in the world.

metas.name: Gunda
metas.description: Captures a farm animal's inner life opening up when a film refuses to narrate it. Black and white, no music, no dialogue: a sow and her piglets, chickens and cows, at their own pace and eye level.

metas.name: All That Breathes
metas.description: Captures caring for creatures everyone else steps over as a way of holding a world together. Two brothers in Delhi run a makeshift hospital for black kites falling out of a polluted sky while the city frays around them.

metas.name: Chasing Ice
metas.description: Captures climate change made visible at human time-scale, no argument required. Time-lapse cameras planted on glaciers play back years of retreat in seconds — including a calving event the size of a city district, caught by chance.

metas.name: The Salt of the Earth
metas.description: Captures what a lifetime of looking at suffering does to a person, and one answer to it. Photographer Sebastião Salgado walks through forty years of famine, war and exodus in his own images, then turns to restoring a dead forest — and it works.

metas.name: Particle Fever
metas.description: Captures big science's actual emotional texture: boredom, terror, and a party when the bump appears in the data. The Large Hadron Collider's first runs filmed from inside the collaboration, theorists not knowing if thirty years of work is about to collapse.

metas.name: The Farthest
metas.description: Captures the most optimistic object our species has ever made, and the scientists ageing alongside it. The Voyager probes, told by the people who built them, carrying a golden record of human greetings out of the solar system.

metas.name: Good Night Oppy
metas.description: Captures engineers grieving a machine, completely sincerely, and earning it. Mars rover Opportunity, built for 90 days, worked for 15 years; the JPL team's attachment stops being a joke about anthropomorphism around year ten.

metas.name: AlphaGo
metas.description: Captures the exact historical moment a machine did something its makers couldn't explain. DeepMind's system against Lee Sedol in Seoul, filmed in both camps; Move 37 lands and the human experts go quiet.

metas.name: Lo and Behold: Reveries of the Connected World
metas.description: Captures the internet as something stranger and more fragile than either its utopians or critics describe. Herzog wanders its birthplace, a monastery of monks with smartphones, a family hounded by trolls, and asks if the network dreams of itself.

metas.name: The Atomic Cafe
metas.director: Jayne Loader, Kevin Rafferty, Pierce Rafferty
metas.description: Captures a state lying to its citizens in its own cheerful voice. Nothing but 1940s–50s American government films, ads and newsreels about the bomb, cut together with no narration: duck and cover, soldiers reassured about fallout.

metas.name: They Shall Not Grow Old
metas.description: Captures the trenches suddenly populated by recognisable young men instead of ghosts. Peter Jackson restores jerky silent WWI footage to correct speed, colourises it, and adds voices reconstructed from veterans' interviews and lip-reading.

metas.name: A Film Unfinished
metas.description: Captures how a fabricated archive keeps passing as truth until someone watches it slowly enough. A Nazi propaganda film shot in the Warsaw Ghetto is taken apart shot by shot, including outtakes where the staging shows.

metas.name: Winter on Fire: Ukraine's Fight for Freedom
metas.description: Captures a protest becoming a revolution in real time, and what it costs the people who refuse to leave. Kyiv's Euromaidan over 93 days, from student demonstration to a government shooting its own citizens, filmed inside the square.

metas.name: 13th
metas.description: Captures the essay-documentary at maximum force — a thesis you can feel being assembled. DuVernay builds one chain from the Thirteenth Amendment's exception clause through convict leasing, Jim Crow and the war on drugs to mass incarceration.

metas.name: Inside Job
metas.description: Captures elite impunity as a tone of voice. The 2008 financial crisis explained with unusual clarity and barely suppressed fury, including interviews where the architects keep incriminating themselves with total calm.

metas.name: Paradise Lost: The Child Murders at Robin Hood Hills
metas.description: Captures a Satanic-panic prosecution from the inside; the film itself became evidence in the decades-long fight over the case. Three Arkansas teenagers convicted of murder largely for liking Metallica and black clothes, filmed through the trial with access to every family.

metas.name: Searching for Sugar Man
metas.description: Captures fame existing in full, in a place the famous person never knew about. Detroit singer Rodriguez, a flop at home in the 1970s and rumoured dead, was bigger than Elvis in apartheid South Africa. The most joyful film in its batch.
